extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, USPTO supervisory staff, patent owners and third-party requesters / patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for USPTO personnel on deciding whether to order ex parte reexamination of a patent (including timeframes, substantive standards for a "substantial new question of patentability," handling second requests, transfers, and litigation-related procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of entry for papers about examiner assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper alerting the Office to the assignment of a reexamination to the 'original examiner' does not itself have a right of entry under the rules; a third party who becomes aware of such assignment cannot file a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 if the patent owner has not filed a statement under 37 CFR 1.530.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In situations where a paper directed to the examiner assignment has no right of entry under the rules, the Office may waive the rules to the extent that the paper will be entered and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedure between CRU art units
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CRU Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE) believes a reexamination should be assigned to another art unit, the SPE must obtain consent of the target CRU SPE and hand-carry the file; unresolved conflicts are resolved by the CRU Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All transfers should be handled expeditiously (special dispatch per 35 U.S.C. 305); if the 'new' art unit accepts, its CRU SPE assigns the request to an examiner in that unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time reporting for reexamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel must report all time spent on reexamination activities on individual Time and Attendance Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities such as supervision, copying, typing, and docketing; accurate time reporting is essential because reexamination fees are based on full cost recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated reexamination authority and rarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may initiate ex parte reexamination at any time during patent enforceability if a substantial new question of patentability is determined, and may do so without a request or fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director-initiated reexamination is rare and only in compelling circumstances after review of all facts; authority may be delegated to Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy or exercised by the Director, Deputy Director, or Commissioner for Patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month statutory decision period
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following filing of a request for reexamination, the Director (or an examiner per 37 CFR 1.515) must determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should take up a request about 6 weeks after filing and mail the decision within 10 weeks; if the 3-month period ends on a weekend/holiday, mail by preceding business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC litigation search before determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before determining whether to reexamine, the examiner must request a litigation search by the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) to check patent litigation involvement and record results on the reexamination IFW file jacket form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If litigation is or was involved, include reference to any paper filed and notify/bring to attention of the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) SPE; guidance on additional searches may be obtained from Office of the Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims in effect govern determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's determination is based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination; certain amendments (e.g., presented with the request by the owner or filed in pending reexamination) will not be considered when deciding requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No input from the patent owner is considered prior to determination unless the owner filed the request; amendments in reissue or pending reexamination may be excluded per statute and regulation references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of the decision — order vs. claim rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on the request is whether to grant or deny an order for reexamination based on whether a substantial new question of patentability is found; the examiner SHOULD NOT reject claims in the order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection of claims will be made in the first Office action on patentability issued after expiration of the time for submitting the patent owner’s statement and requester’s reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial positions in the order
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should indicate, insofar as possible, an initial position on all issues identified in the request or by the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows the patent owner’s statement and requester’s reply to address the examiner’s initial positions during the subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art patent or printed publication raises an SNQ where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding whether the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is sufficient that at least one claim be affected; the same question must not have been previously decided by final judicial invalidity or prior Office examination/reexamination; a prima facie case of unpatentability is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior final or Office decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An SNQ is not raised if the same question of patentability has already been decided by (A) a final holding of invalidity after all appeals, or (B) by the Office in a previous examination or pending reexamination of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check the patent file history to ascertain whether the prior art was previously cited/considered ('old art').

rubrics_metrics.name: Pertinency and manner-of-application requirement (35 U.S.C. 302 / 37 CFR 1.510(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims and a filing date may not be awarded for the request; failure to set forth applicability to a claim generally means that claim will not be reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination scope limited to claims requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office’s determination and subsequent examination will generally be limited to review of the claims for which reexamination was requested; claims not requested will generally not be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office chooses to reexamine claims not requested, it is permitted to do so; case law (e.g., Sony) shows reexamination can be limited to requested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent requests must present a 'different' SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent request filed while a first reexamination is pending must provide prior art that raises a substantial new question of patentability that is different from that raised in the pending reexamination for the claims in effect at the time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the second request raises the same SNQ as the pending proceeding, it should be denied; if it raises a different SNQ as to some claims, it may be granted in part; the decision is based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of new/amended claims in pending reexamination by subsequent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a subsequent request provides a different SNQ for the claims in effect, it may also provide information directed to proposed new or amended claims in the pending reexamination to permit examination of the entire patent package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents patentees from nominally amending claims to preclude later challenges and avoids unnecessary serial filings; information directed to proposed new/amended claims is addressed during the later-filed reexamination where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment and petition under 37 CFR 1.182
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second or subsequent request appears to have been filed for purposes of harassment and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (filed as part of or as the statement) is granted, prosecution on the second/subsequent reexamination may be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merger with pending proceedings that would unduly prolong reexamination and conflict with special dispatch may be avoided if harassment is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'old art' (previously cited/considered) after Public Law 107-273 (Nov 2, 2002)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on previously cited/considered art ('old art') does not necessarily preclude an SNQ for reexamination ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002; determinations are fact-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Old art may form an SNQ if it is presented/viewed in a new light or with a material new argument or interpretation. When SNQ is based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01 in the order explaining the old art basis and why it raises an SNQ; include specifics and examiner notes as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to find prima facie unpatentability
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that a prima facie case of unpatentability exist to find that a substantial new question of patentability is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SNQ could be present even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim as fully anticipated or obvious in view of the prior art; see In re Etter for discussion of the difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of requests when patent reissued or reissue issued after request
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after a reissue patent for that patent has already issued, reexamination will be denied because the original patent has been surrendered; to reexamine, a new request based on the reissue patent must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue issues after filing of a request, see MPEP § 2285 for proper handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and reviewability of determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination by the Director that no substantial new question of patentability has been raised is final and nonappealable, though the requester may petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 within one month of mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely petition is filed or the petition affirms refusal, the determination is final and nonappealable; there is limited case law nuance about judicial review of grants vs denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner practice on describing the basis of the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on the request should discuss all patent claims requested for reexamination and limit discussion to whether an SNQ has been raised; the examiner should indicate initial positions on issues identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not issue rejections in the order; provide sufficient explanation so patent owner and requester can respond effectively in their subsequent submissions.
